scenes.heading: End-of-year exam technique
scenes.sub: Answer the question that was asked
scenes.say: The end-of-year Biology exam is full of new organisms, new experiments and new data. It tests whether you can apply what you know, not just recall it. Here's how to pick up every mark you can.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: 'Dice the onion' and 'caramelise the onion' need different actions
scenes.breaks: a cook can taste and adjust, but the assessor only sees what you wrote, so check your answer against the command word.
scenes.say: A recipe that says dice the onion wants something different from one that says caramelise it. Command words work the same way. Describe asks what happens. Explain asks why or how. Evaluate wants a judgement backed by evidence. And the marks are the serving size: about one distinct idea per mark.

scenes.heading: Extended responses
scenes.say: For an extended response, plan for thirty seconds first. Write in a logical order: cause, process, effect. Use precise terms like clonal expansion or allele frequency. Name the organism or molecule from the scenario. Then re-read the question to check you answered every part.

scenes.heading: Data question: TDI
scenes.question: Resistant bacteria were 2% in year 1, 10% in year 3 and 45% in year 5 of heavy antibiotic use. Analyse.
lines: Data: 2% in year 1 to 45% in year 5
scenes.say: For data, use T D I: trend, data, interpretation. Resistant bacteria rose from two percent in year one to forty-five percent in year five, fastest between years three and five. The antibiotic was a selection pressure, so the resistance allele became more common.
scenes.caption: For data, use TDI: trend, data, interpretation. Resistant bacteria rose from 2% in year 1 to 45% in year 5, fastest between years 3 and 5. The antibiotic was a selection pressure, so the resistance allele became more common.

scenes.heading: Experimental design
points: Dependent: what you measure, with units
scenes.say: Know your variables precisely. The independent variable is what you change. The dependent variable is what you measure, stated with units. Controlled variables stay the same. And a control group gives a baseline. DRY MIX: dependent and responding on the y-axis, manipulated and independent on the x-axis.

scenes.heading: Accuracy vs precision
scenes.say: Picture a dartboard. Darts on the bullseye are accurate. Darts tightly clustered are precise. You can be precise without being accurate. And when you suggest an improvement, change it and say why.

scenes.heading: Your revision plan
points: Turn key knowledge into a checklist
Keep an error log and review it
scenes.say: In the final weeks, turn the key knowledge into a checklist. Do past exams under timed conditions and mark them with the examiners' reports. Keep an error log of your mistakes, and review it before each practice exam. Check the current VCAA specifications for exact exam details.

points: Name the bug: stay in context
scenes.say: Quick recap. Circle the command word. Use the marks as a guide. For data, use trend, data, interpretation. And above all, answer the question that was asked, about the scenario that was given. Now try the practice questions!
